text: half my friends say they're sitting this one out. I get it, but it's frustrating
I used to skip midterms. then my city council race was decided by 31 votes. never again
honestly don't see the point in voting in midterms when nothing changes either way
I don't care which party fixes it, I care that my insurance premium went up 22% this year. that's my midterm issue
groceries up again and every ad I see is about something else. who is actually talking about rent this cycle
interesting that the local races in my district are almost entirely about housing permits and property taxes
signed up to be a poll worker this year. they need people everywhere, it pays, and you get a sticker
the misinformation about mail ballots in my feed this week is wild. go to your state's official site, not screenshots
my county clerk did a livestream walking through how ballots are counted. surprisingly reassuring, highly recommend
seeing a lot of fake 'you can vote by text' posts again. you cannot vote by text. report them
healthcare is coming up more than I expected in the local debates. mostly prescription costs
my mom's medication costs are the only thing she wants to hear candidates talk about and nobody is
both campaigns here are running immigration ads that feel designed to scare people rather than inform them
immigration is the top issue in every ad in my area, which is interesting because it barely came up at the town hall
don't skip the down-ballot races. judges, sheriffs, and school boards affect your daily life more than congress
the school board race in my town is way more interesting than any of the national stuff. actual policy debates!
went to a candidate forum at the library. 80 people showed up on a tuesday night. democracy is alive in small rooms
every conversation about the midterms with family turns into a fight within 5 minutes. thanksgiving is going to be fun
exhausted by campaign texts. I've gotten 40 this week from both sides and I'm already voting
the attack ads in my state are so nasty I genuinely can't tell what either candidate wants to do
house forecasts have been moving a lot this month. worth remembering most polls have a 3-4 point margin of error
the generic ballot polling is basically tied, which means turnout in like 6 states decides everything
I stopped looking at polls in 2016 and my blood pressure has never been better
new district maps mean a lot of people are voting for a different rep than last time. look up your district before you go
my town got split into three districts. none of the candidates have ever been here
fun fact: midterm turnout has historically been 15-20 points lower than presidential years
just registered to vote for the first time! took 4 minutes online. if you're 18+ do it
early voting starts next week in my county and the poll worker training was packed. good sign
our campus registration drive signed up 1,200 students this week. young people are paying attention
reminder: registration deadlines vary by state and some are this week. check yours
